My family has farmed this land for three generations. My father taught me, and his father taught him. I know this land. The soil here is loamy, the water table is reachable, and the North China Plain has one answer for people like me: **wheat in winter, corn in summer**. That is what I grow. That is what everyone here grows. I have about 10 mu.

I will plant winter wheat come October. I already know which variety — I buy the improved seed from the same supply shop I always go to, the one my neighbor also uses. Last year it yielded well. I will apply base fertilizer before sowing — diammonium phosphate mixed with urea, the way I have always done — and top-dress with urea at jointing. I will irrigate at overwintering, green-up, jointing, and heading. Four times. That is what the wheat needs here, there is not enough rain. I spray herbicide early, then fungicide before heading for rust. Two, maybe three sprays.

After wheat harvest in June, I sow corn immediately. Same fields. I use hybrid corn seed, the kind that yields heavy. I apply fertilizer at sowing and again at big bell stage. Rain helps more in summer so maybe one or two irrigations only. I spray once for borer if I see it.

I use rotary tillage — easier on my back, faster, and my son helps me only on weekends now. I do not deep plough every year.
